slides.texte_overlay:
5 posture mistakes that
make you look nervous
Mistake 1: sitting on the edge of the chair. It looks like you're ready to run. Sit back, use the backrest, take up your seat. Relaxed sitting says you're comfortable being there.
Mistake 2: shifting your weight from foot to foot. It reads as restless and impatient. Plant both feet a little apart and stay still. Grounded stance, calm presence.
Mistake 3: holding your drink or phone in front of your chest. It's a shield, and people feel it. Hold things at your side or waist height, and your whole body looks more open.
Mistake 4: tilting your head down when you talk. Your voice gets muffled and you look unsure. Keep your chin level, like there's a string pulling the top of your head up.
Mistake 5: walking fast everywhere. Rushing looks anxious, even when you're just late. Walk a little slower than you think you should. Unhurried movement always reads as confident.
Calm the mind, and the body follows. Five minutes a day of history, art or science gives your head something steady to focus on, and that calm shows in how you stand.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: tense shoulders and a busy head. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Calm mind, calm body, and it shows in how I stand.

slides.texte_overlay: The fix: notice it once an hour. Set a quiet reminder for a week. Every time it buzzes, check your feet, shoulders and chin. After seven days, good posture starts happening on its own.
